description_full: Electricity Generating Public Company Limited, together with its subsidiaries, generates and sells electricity to government sector and industrial users primarily in Thailand, Laos, the Philippines, Indonesia, Australia, South Korea, Taiwan, and the United States. It operates through Electricity Generation and Other Businesses segments. The company generates electricity from various resources, such as biomass, hydropower, solar and wind power, battery energy, and fuel cell. It also involved in operation, maintenance, engineering and construction services to power plants, petrochemical plants, oil refineries and other industries; coal mining, management, and oil pipeline business. The company was incorporated in 1992 and is based in Bangkok, Thailand.
ceo_bio: Mr. Tawatchai  Sumranwanich | President & Director | Age 51 | Compensation: $4,762 (FY2025)
financial_summary: ELECTRICITY GENERATING PUBLIC C is a mid-cap utilities business with a $2.3B market cap on $956M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -17% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.3pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 16% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $92M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.74× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 16.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
